findings: The observable is unconditioned excited-state population. In the stated weak-coupling zero-temperature limit its decay counts both radiative escape and irreversible transfer to the passive substrate.

The Fresnel Green-tensor factors have the correct normal and tangential dipole weights. The w-to-v continuation of the vacuum longitudinal wavevector gives positive-imaginary evanescent integrands with the stated exp(-i omega t) convention.

For real positive epsilon<=1 the vacuum-evanescent sector is also evanescent in the material, so its Fresnel reflection is real and its decay contribution is exactly zero. The transparent calibration therefore remains exactly shared while testing nontrivial propagating interference.

The independent reference constructs transmitted TE/TM electric fields, integrates material Joule heating through the half-space depth, and adds upward radiation. Its direct/reflected polarization signs and azimuthal normalization agree with Maxwell boundary conditions.

The public specification fixes the local material response, no separate surface sheet, zero bath temperature, leading exponential limit and population detector. It neither supplies the missing sector formula nor mandates a numerical representation.
